source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; O. Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies a refusal-related direction in LLM activations, not superposition, feature sparsity, capacity competition, or the geometry of features that are superposed. Its results therefore do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports causal interventions on a refusal direction and measurements related to its expression. These concern a different feature and behavior from superposition. Direction-selection scores are used to select an intervention and are not outcome rows. Safety-score plots alongside refusal-score plots are not included where they do not disagree with the refusal results; the separately tabulated safety score is included because Table 10 compares it with refusal score.
record.test_reason: The paper finds one difference-in-means direction per chat model that mediates refusal. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background for the idea that features are linear directions. It does not measure feature sparsity, overlap of features in fewer dimensions, capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, SAE features, or 1-D versus multi-dimensional features under superposition. The single-direction result is about linear causal mediation of one behaviour, not about what is superposed, so it does not test V6 either.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace across 13 open-source chat models (1.8B–72B). Ablating the direction disables refusal, and adding it induces refusal. A rank-one weight orthogonalization yields a white-box jailbreak with little capability loss, apart from TruthfulQA drops. In Qwen 1.8B, an adversarial suffix suppresses the refusal direction by redirecting the attention of key heads. They also report the direction is already present in base models. They note the direction's semantics are unclear, possibly 'harm' rather than refusal. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive harmful/harmless instructions to extract a refusal direction and intervenes on LLM activations; it does not use the original toy-network setup or test feature sparsity and superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports substantial system-prompt sensitivity for orthogonalized Llama-2 models in the HarmBench jailbreak evaluation; this concerns jailbreak success, not the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In 13 open chat models, ablating one difference-in-means direction cuts refusal on harmful prompts. Adding the same direction induces refusal on harmless prompts. For Llama-3 8B, ablation drops refusal score from 0.95 to 0.01 and safety score from 0.97 to 0.15.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single linear residual-stream direction causally mediates refusal in safety-tuned chat LLMs (linear representation / one-dimensional mediation of a behaviour).

record.problems: The authors say the direction-extraction method relies on heuristics and is not necessarily optimal. The adversarial-suffix analysis is limited to one model and one suffix. Figure 1 and Figure 3 values are presented graphically rather than numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1's safety-score series was not separately rowed because the paper describes it alongside refusal score without reporting a disagreement. Other results, including adversarial-suffix cosine plots (Figure 5), component analyses (Figure 6), and base-model cosine plots (Figure 24), concern the refusal mechanism and not superposition or feature-capacity claims.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, no sparsity sweep, no geometry of superposed features.
All: no analysis of neurons, capacity, or feature importance.
All: polysemantic neurons are not examined.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons and no dictionary or SAE recovery. Only a supervised contrastive direction is used.
All: no SAE features are trained or evaluated.

Whether superposed features are 1-D. The paper shows a single direction is causally sufficient and necessary for refusal, but does not test superposition or compare against multi-dimensional alternatives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'discusses' overstates the link. The superposition paper appears only in a citation list supporting features-as-directions, so the relation is changed to cites_only. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']; no row fixes needed. F1 and F3 values are figure-only, but the text states the direction of effect. The Appendix J base-model cosine result and the §5 suffix analysis are reasonably left out as irrelevant to the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, or show sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether they indicate superposition.
Whether features are distributed across many neurons or sparse features can be recovered with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representations.
Whether features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
